questions.q: Which four components define every ledger in Oracle Fusion General Ledger?
options: Chart of accounts, accounting calendar, currency, and accounting method
Chart of accounts, journal source, journal category, and currency
Legal entity, business unit, data access set, and currency
Primary ledger, secondary ledger, ledger set, and reporting currency
questions.explain: The four C's — chart of accounts, calendar, currency, and accounting method — define every ledger.

questions.q: After a ledger is saved, which of its four defining components can still be changed?
options: The currency
The accounting method
The chart of accounts
The accounting calendar
questions.explain: Chart of accounts, calendar, and currency are locked once saved. Only the accounting method can still change.

questions.q: What distinguishes a secondary ledger from a reporting currency?
options: A reporting currency is independent; a secondary ledger is just a currency conversion
They are two names for the same structure
A secondary ledger is an independent set of books; a reporting currency just restates the primary ledger in another currency
A secondary ledger can only be used for statistics, never for accounting balances
questions.explain: A secondary ledger is its own ledger, potentially with a different COA or method. A reporting currency is not independent — it mirrors the primary ledger's structure in another currency.

questions.q: What does a ledger set do?
options: It stores its own independent balances separate from its member ledgers
It converts a secondary ledger into a primary ledger
It defines the accounting method for a new ledger
It groups ledgers that share a chart of accounts and calendar so you can operate on them together
questions.explain: A ledger set is a convenience grouping for ledgers sharing a chart of accounts and calendar — it has no balances of its own.

questions.q: In this course's running example, what is Solara Fixtures, Inc.?
options: A real Oracle customer referenced in Oracle's documentation
A fictional example company used for worked scenarios throughout the course
The name of Oracle's demo chart of accounts
A secondary ledger used only for statutory reporting
questions.explain: Solara Fixtures, Inc. is a clearly-labeled fictional company invented for this course's worked examples.
